stem.text: The function h is twice differentiable at every x in the closed interval \( [-5, 0] \), with \( h'(-2) = 0 \) and \( h''(-2) > 0 \). Must h attain an absolute minimum value on the closed interval \( [-5, 0] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, because h is differentiable, so continuous, on the closed interval \( [-5, 0] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem applies.

worked_solution.text: The interval \( [-5, 0] \) is closed and bounded.
The function h is differentiable, so continuous, on the closed interval \( [-5, 0] \).
Both hypotheses of the Extreme Value Theorem hold, so h attains an absolute minimum value on \( [-5, 0] \). The theorem gives existence only, not where the value occurs.
